Executive Summary

Recommended migration path: Re-architect. Derived from synthesis of 62 prior signals across INV, STATE, DATA, CTX, SBOM, TF, EGR, CRYPTO, DYN, and COMP prefixes. The workload carries 3 critical signals (DATA-05, CTX-01, CTX-02), 12 high signals, and 16 medium signals. Critical blockers include plaintext fallback when ENCRYPTION_KEY is absent (CTX-05), direct PHI/PII routing to external Anthropic API (CTX-06), and unencrypted PII at rest across multiple CRM tables (DATA-01, DATA-02, DATA-03). SAST/DAST are entirely absent (CTX-03). Dependency CVEs are confirmed high/critical (SBOM-01). The application is NOT ready for simple Rehost or Replatform. Significant Re-architect work is required to resolve sovereign data residency, encryption-at-rest, and third-party AI egress before cloud migration is safe. Verdict: Re-architect.

Key constraint: Key constraint synthesis: The combination of CTX-05 (ENCRYPTION_KEY plaintext fallback), CTX-06 (direct PHI routing to Anthropic api.anthropic.com with no sovereign proxy), and DATA-05 (critical data exposure) constitutes a hard sovereign-residency blocker. Any cloud migration landing zone — including AWS sovereign regions — cannot compensate for application-layer plaintext data paths and uncontrolled third-party AI egress. These three signals together form the primary migration blocker cluster. Additionally, CTX-04 confirms the AWS landing zone snapshot is fabricated (fabricated: true), meaning no validated landing zone exists. SBOM-01 CVEs and CTX-03 absence of SAST/DAST form secondary blockers that must be resolved during re-architecture. Portability is constrained by EGR-01 (no egress domains detected — manual review needed) and TF-03 (no Kubernetes, Docker Compose only). Migration cannot proceed to any cloud without resolving the plaintext fallback and AI egress architectural patterns first.

GDPR_Art_5_1_a Partial Lawfulness, fairness and transparency (Art 5(1)(a))

Document the lawful basis for each processing operation; publish privacy notices in plain language; remove covert tracking.

Assessment

The application documents explicit consent recording at signup, audit logging via data_access_log, and consent endpoints for health records (DATA-07, CTX-13), indicating some transparency and lawfulness mechanisms. However, no cookie consent or privacy control UI was detected across 80 crawled screens (DYN-08), and no privacy notice or transparency information delivery is evidenced in signals, undermining the transparency requirement of Art 5(1)(a). Additionally, the silent fallback to plaintext storage when ENCRYPTION_KEY is absent (CTX-05) raises fairness concerns for self-hosted deployments.

GDPR_Art_5_1_f Fail Integrity and confidentiality (security principle) (Art 5(1)(f))

Trace evidence to Art 32 sub-controls; close any technical-control gap surfaced in Art 32 family.

Assessment

Multiple critical security deficiencies undermine the integrity and confidentiality principle: secrets are stored only in .env files with no rotation or audit trail (CTX-02), SAST/DAST are absent for a health data application (CTX-03), encryption silently degrades to plaintext when ENCRYPTION_KEY is absent (CTX-05), and health data including biomarkers is transmitted to a third-party AI API without documented safeguards (CTX-06). While defense-in-depth layers exist at runtime (CTX-12), the foundational secrets management and encryption assurance gaps are severe for Art 9 health data.

GDPR_Art_23 Fail Restrictions (Art 23)

Identify the specific restricting law for the workload's jurisdiction; document where Art 12-22 rights are constrained and why.

Assessment

Art. 23 concerns Union or Member State legislative measures restricting data subject rights — this is a legislative obligation on lawmakers, not on controllers or processors. No signal suggests the workload is operating under a specific national derogation that would require implementation of Art. 23 controls. This control is not applicable to the controller's technical or organisational responsibilities.

GDPR_Art_24 Partial Responsibility of the controller (Art 24)

GDPR_Art_45 Fail Transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision (Art 45)

Identify which transfers benefit from an adequacy decision; monitor for adequacy-decision changes (Schrems precedent).

Assessment

The USA does not have a blanket adequacy decision covering all transfers; the EU-US Data Privacy Framework applies only to certified organisations. No signal confirms that Anthropic is DPF-certified or that any adequacy basis is relied upon for the transfer of health data to the Anthropic API documented in CTX-06. The transfer therefore cannot be justified on adequacy grounds as evidenced by available signals.

Enable encryption at rest for all storage containing sensitive or personal data; ensure keys are held in a managed key store separate from the data.

Assessment

Multiple signals confirm sensitive and personal data — including PII, health biomarkers, MFA secrets, and biometric captures — is stored without verified at-rest encryption. DATA-01 and DATA-02 note that comment-level claims of app-layer encryption are unsubstantiated by any visible implementation. CTX-05 documents that when ENCRYPTION_KEY is absent, data is silently stored in plaintext, and CRYPTO-02 confirms no at-rest database encryption is configured at the application layer; volume encryption depends on unverified host configuration.

7 signal(s) linked: DATA-01DATA-02DATA-03DATA-04CTX-02CTX-05CRYPTO-02 view all 7
BSI_C5_CRY-03 Fail Key rotation and lifecycle management

Configure automated key rotation in the key management service; define rotation intervals per key type; test rotation procedures annually.

Assessment

CTX-02 explicitly states there is no rotation schedule and no audit trail for secret access, with the ENCRYPTION_KEY stored in .env files on the VPS alongside the data it protects. DATA-04 notes that column naming implies encryption of MFA secrets but no key management or rotation reference is observable. No documented or tested key rotation procedure exists for any cryptographic material in the system.

3 signal(s) linked: CTX-02DATA-04INV-17 view all 3
BSI_C5_COS-01 Partial Network segmentation and zone architecture

Define and implement network security zones; enforce zone boundaries with firewalls or security groups; document the zone architecture and review annually.

Assessment

INV-13 confirms Docker and STACKIT networks are declared via Terraform, and CTX-12 references Cloudflare WAF as a perimeter layer and Row-Level Security on 15 tables as an internal segmentation mechanism. However, STATE-04 confirms deployment topology is unknown, no evidence of formal zone architecture or documented traffic filtering between zones is present, and CTX-15 indicates a single VPS deployment without clear separation of production from development environments.

5 signal(s) linked: INV-13CTX-12CTX-15STATE-04INV-05 view all 5
BSI_C5_OPS-01 Partial Change management process for cloud infrastructure

Implement a change management workflow with mandatory approval gates; enforce through the CI/CD pipeline; retain change records for audit.

Assessment

CTX-17 references a backup script and Terraform secrets module, and INV-15/INV-16 show infrastructure managed via Terraform/OpenTofu indicating some infrastructure-as-code discipline. However, CTX-04 and CTX-16 reveal a direct version contradiction between declared infrastructure state and application requirements (PostgreSQL 15.6 vs 16), demonstrating that changes are not fully validated before production. No formal change management process, approval workflow, or emergency change procedure is documented in any signal.

4 signal(s) linked: CTX-04CTX-16INV-15INV-16 view all 4
BSI_C5_OPS-02 Partial Patch and vulnerability management

Establish patch SLAs by severity (critical: 72 hours, high: 7 days); automate patch deployment where possible; track exceptions in the risk register.

Assessment

CTX-03 confirms cargo audit (dependency CVE scanning) runs in CI, providing some vulnerability identification coverage. SBOM-01 identifies at least one high/critical CVE in runtime Node.js dependencies from a limited spot check. However, CTX-03 also confirms SAST and DAST are not configured, no defined maximum patching timeframe is documented, and patch application status tracking is not evidenced.

3 signal(s) linked: CTX-03SBOM-01SBOM-02 view all 3
BSI_C5_OPS-03 Partial Capacity and performance management

Implement capacity monitoring dashboards with alerting at defined thresholds; conduct quarterly capacity reviews; document forecasts.

Assessment

CTX-07 explicitly states that VPS vCPU, RAM, disk, and per-container resource usage are not captured in documentation. CTX-15 notes the Terraform compute module targets min/max replicas for horizontal scaling, suggesting some capacity planning intent. However, no capacity monitoring, performance baselines, or documented peak usage planning are evidenced.

2 signal(s) linked: CTX-07CTX-15 view all 2
BSI_C5_OPS-04 Partial Asset management -- inventory of information assets

Implement a CMDB or equivalent asset register covering all cloud service components; update it on every infrastructure change; review completeness quarterly.

Assessment

INV-01 through INV-17 collectively demonstrate a broad asset inventory derived from Terraform state covering compute, networking, storage, Kubernetes, object storage, and secrets management. However, INV-01 notes that full static analysis is only available for Node.js/TypeScript, and CTX-08 lists several planned integrations not yet implemented, indicating the asset inventory may not reflect the actual future state. No evidence of a defined review interval or formal inventory management process is present.

11 signal(s) linked: INV-01INV-05INV-10INV-11INV-12INV-13INV-14INV-15INV-16INV-17CTX-08 view all 11
BSI_C5_OPS-05 Partial Security configuration baseline and hardening

Define hardening baselines per system type; enforce via IaC; run continuous compliance scanning and alert on drift.

Assessment

CTX-12 documents eight security layers including Cloudflare WAF, TLS 1.3, Argon2id, RLS, and rate limiting, indicating meaningful hardening has been applied at the application layer. However, CTX-02 reveals secrets are stored in plain .env files rather than a hardened secrets management system, CTX-05 documents a silent plaintext fallback for encryption, and no reference to a recognised hardening standard (e.g., CIS Benchmarks) or systematic configuration compliance monitoring is present.

4 signal(s) linked: CTX-12CTX-02CTX-05CTX-03 view all 4
BSI_C5_OPS-06 Partial Logging and monitoring strategy

Define logging requirements per event category; centralise logs in a tamper-evident store; configure retention per regulatory requirements; establish a review cadence.

Assessment

CTX-13 references pgaudit and a data_access_log for GDPR Art. 15 compliance, and TF-04 confirms structured logging via the Rust tracing crate. However, CTX-02 confirms there is no audit trail for secret access, no evidence of log tamper protection, defined retention periods, or a documented logging and monitoring strategy covering security incident review is present.

4 signal(s) linked: CTX-13TF-04CTX-02CTX-12 view all 4
BSI_C5_AVL-01 Fail Business continuity plan covering cloud services

Author and maintain a cloud-specific BCP; test it at least annually through a tabletop exercise; document and act on test findings.

Assessment

CTX-01 documents no off-site automated backup, no scheduled daily backup, and no backup restore test procedure. STATE-04 confirms deployment topology and SPOF risk are unknown. No signals reference a documented, approved, or tested business continuity plan covering the cloud service, escalation paths, or communication procedures.

3 signal(s) linked: CTX-01STATE-04CTX-15 view all 3
BSI_C5_AVL-02 Fail Recovery time and recovery point objectives defined and tested

Document RTO and RPO per service tier; conduct recovery tests at least annually; close gaps between tested recovery times and defined objectives.

Assessment

CTX-15 notes container restart policy provides RTO < 1 min for container crashes, which is informal rather than a formally defined and BIA-derived RTO. CTX-01 confirms no scheduled backup exists, making RPO effectively undefined and untested. No signals reference formal RTO/RPO definitions based on business impact analysis or contractual commitments, nor evidence of recovery capability testing.

3 signal(s) linked: CTX-01CTX-15STATE-04 view all 3
BSI_C5_AVL-03 Fail Geographic redundancy and failover capability

Deploy across at least two availability zones in a compliant geographic region; test failover annually; confirm data residency alignment with DAT-02.

Assessment

CTX-15 confirms the application is currently deployed on a single Hetzner VPS, representing a single point of failure with no geographic redundancy. INV-15 shows a STACKIT SKE cluster declared in Terraform state, suggesting future multi-region intent, but no evidence of active geographic distribution or tested failover mechanisms is present. CTX-11 documents data residency routing but this does not constitute geographic redundancy for availability purposes.

4 signal(s) linked: CTX-15INV-15CTX-11STATE-04 view all 4
BSI_C5_AVL-04 Fail Backup strategy and restore testing

Implement automated backup with offsite or cross-account storage; test restores quarterly; document the backup schedule and retain test results.

Assessment

CTX-01 explicitly documents no off-site automated backup, no scheduled daily backup, and no backup restore test procedure; backups are only taken pre-deploy and retained locally on the VPS. CTX-17 notes the backup script is 'not yet implemented.' INV-16 shows object storage buckets declared (including a backups bucket) in Terraform, but these are not confirmed as actively used for backups.

3 signal(s) linked: CTX-01CTX-17INV-16 view all 3
BSI_C5_DEV-02 Partial Secure software development lifecycle

Document SSDLC practices including threat modelling and security testing gates; enforce via CI pipeline; train developers on secure coding.

Assessment

CTX-12 documents defense-in-depth security controls applied at the application layer, and DATA-06 through DATA-09 show GDPR-related security controls implemented with E2E test coverage. However, CTX-03 confirms SAST is not configured, no threat modelling evidence is present in any signal, and CTX-08 shows several security-relevant features (SSO, OAuth) are designed but not yet implemented, indicating security requirements are not consistently addressed from design through deployment.

6 signal(s) linked: CTX-12CTX-03DATA-06DATA-07DATA-08CTX-08 view all 6
BSI_C5_DEV-03 Fail Code review and security testing before release

Gate releases on SAST scan completion; block critical findings; retain scan artefacts in the release record.

Assessment

CTX-03 explicitly confirms SAST and DAST are both 'None / Not configured', meaning security testing is absent from the release pipeline. Only cargo audit (dependency CVE scanning) and Playwright E2E auth flow tests run in CI. SBOM-01 identifies at least one high/critical CVE found even from a limited spot check, demonstrating that existing controls are insufficient to catch security issues before release.

3 signal(s) linked: CTX-03SBOM-01DATA-10 view all 3
BSI_C5_PI-02 Partial Data subject rights fulfilment process

Define a data subject rights handling procedure; assign ownership; log all requests and responses; train customer-facing staff on obligations.

Assessment

Several data subject rights are implemented: GDPR Art. 15 (access) is covered by a JSON export endpoint and a regression test guard (DATA-08), Art. 17 (erasure) is implemented via soft-delete and hard purge in purge.rs (DATA-06), and Art. 7 consent grant/revoke endpoints exist (DATA-07, DATA-09). However, no evidence of a formal log tracking data subject requests and their response timelines is visible in the signals, and rectification and restriction rights are not explicitly evidenced. Additionally, the GDPR export completeness test covers a broad set of health and PII data (DATA-05), but gaps in encryption of underlying data (DATA-01, DATA-02) undermine the integrity of the access process.

8 signal(s) linked: DATA-06DATA-07DATA-08DATA-09DATA-05DATA-01DATA-02CTX-13 view all 8
BSI_C5_PI-03 Partial Encrypted transmission of data

Enforce TLS 1.2+ on all public endpoints; disable weak cipher suites; scan for unencrypted transmission paths quarterly.

Assessment

Transmission security is partially strong: TLS 1.3 via rustls with no OpenSSL dependency is confirmed at the transport layer, and Cloudflare WAF provides an additional perimeter (CTX-12). HMAC-SHA256 is used for MAC operations (CRYPTO-01). However, biomarker data, chat history, and lab documents are transmitted to the Anthropic Claude API (api.anthropic.com), an external third-party endpoint, and no evidence is provided that this channel's cipher suite compliance with BSI TR-02102 has been verified (CTX-06). At-rest encryption is also not reliably enforced (CTX-05, CRYPTO-02), and while this control focuses on transmission, the overall cryptographic posture raises concerns.

Remediation Runbook

  1. Resolve observability gap (PARTIAL)

    Structured logging is confirmed via Rust tracing/tracing-subscriber crates (TF-04), and Gatus is present as a monitoring service (INV-05). However, no signals confirm metrics export, distributed tracing, SLO definitions, alerting rules, or on-call runbooks; BSI C5 shows 0 SATISFIED controls indicating broad observability gaps.

    Addresses: TF-04 INV-05 COMP-02 CTX-15
  2. Resolve testing maturity gap (PARTIAL)

    E2E tests via Playwright are present and cover patient journey and GDPR export completeness (DATA-08, DATA-09), and cargo audit runs in CI (CTX-03). However, SAST and DAST are absent (CTX-03), no signals confirm unit or integration test gating, mutation testing, or performance/load testing, and a hardcoded test credential was found (DATA-10).

    Addresses: CTX-03 DATA-08 DATA-09 DATA-10 COMP-01
  3. Resolve architecture assessment gap (PARTIAL)

    Docker Compose with 4 services is the current deployment model with no Kubernetes manifests present yet a Kubernetes cluster is declared in Terraform state (INV-05, INV-15), indicating a transitional and partially documented topology. No replicas or scaling config is present in Compose (TF-03), deployment topology is unknown (STATE-04), and several planned integrations remain unimplemented (CTX-08, CTX-09), leaving scalability path and service boundaries partially defined.

    Addresses: INV-05 INV-15 TF-03 STATE-04 CTX-08 CTX-09
  4. Resolve database assessment gap (PARTIAL)

    PostgreSQL is used with sqlx (INV-10), object storage buckets for backups exist (INV-16), and GDPR erasure is implemented (DATA-06). However, no off-site automated backup, no restore test procedure, and only local pre-deploy dumps are documented (CTX-01); at-rest encryption is not confirmed in application code and depends on host configuration (CRYPTO-02); and the AWS landing zone references an incompatible PostgreSQL version (CTX-16).

    Addresses: CTX-01 CRYPTO-02 INV-10 INV-16 DATA-06 CTX-16 DATA-01
  5. Resolve integration assessment gap (PARTIAL)

    Stripe webhook secret is referenced but its presence on the VPS is unconfirmed (CTX-10), and the Dr. Alex AI module routes sensitive health data to Anthropic Claude API without documented circuit breakers or egress controls (CTX-06). No egress allow-list or contract testing signals are present (EGR-01), and several integrations including OAuth, SAML, and health-device connectors remain unimplemented (CTX-08).

    Addresses: CTX-06 CTX-10 EGR-01 CTX-08 DYN-04
  6. Resolve iam assessment gap (PARTIAL)

    Strong authentication controls exist including JWT HS256, Argon2id, TOTP MFA, and Row-Level Security on 15 tables (CTX-12), and a secrets manager instance is declared in Terraform state (INV-17). However, all secrets are currently stored in .env files on the VPS with no rotation schedule or audit trail (CTX-02), the ENCRYPTION_KEY passthrough allows plaintext storage in self-hosted deployments (CTX-05), and MFA for admin and RBAC enforcement are not fully evidenced across signals.

    Addresses: CTX-02 CTX-05 CTX-12 INV-17 DATA-04 DATA-10 COMP-01
  7. Resolve dr assessment gap (GAP)

    No off-site automated backup, no scheduled daily backup, and no backup restore test procedure exist per architecture documentation (CTX-01); the GPG backup key is classified critical but the backup script is not yet implemented (CTX-17). The deployment is a single VPS with no multi-AZ or multi-region failover (CTX-15), and no DR runbook or DR test evidence is present in any signal.

Glossary

Methodology

About This Assessment

SWAO (Sovereign Workload Assessment and Onboarding) is an automated tool developed by Accenture to assess whether applications are ready for migration to sovereign cloud platforms.

How to Read This Report

  1. Start with the Executive Summary for the overall risk posture.
  2. Review Signals filtered by severity for immediate action items.
  3. Check Compliance for framework-specific control gaps.
  4. Use the Risk Register to track remediation ownership and timelines.
  5. Consult the Landing Zone Readiness section for blockers before migration.

Severity Levels Explained

Severity Description
Critical Immediate risk to compliance or platform onboarding. Likely an LZR blocker.
High Significant risk -- action required within 30 days.
Medium Moderate risk -- address within 90 days.
Low Minor gap -- address within the next quarter.
Informational Observation only. No immediate action required.
Positive Good practice confirmed. No action needed.

Landing Zone Verdict Guide

Landing zone verdicts appear in the LZ Readiness section and indicate whether a target region or provider meets the active sovereignty requirements.

Verdict Meaning
Ready All sovereign requirements met. Migration can proceed to this region without restrictions.
Ready with Changes Service available but not yet enabled or requires configuration. Apply recommended changes before migrating.
Sovereignty Blocked This region or provider fails the active sovereignty framework requirements. Migration would violate the compliance framework in place.
Blocked A required service is not available in this region or from this provider. Migration cannot proceed until the dependency is resolved.

Migration Strategy Guide (7R)

The 7R migration strategy is derived from the assessment findings by the SYNTH pass. It summarises the recommended approach for migrating this application to the sovereign cloud.

Strategy Description
Retire The application will be decommissioned and removed from the portfolio.
Retain The application remains on-premises or in its current environment with no change.
Rehost The application is lifted-and-shifted to the sovereign cloud with minimal modification.
Replatform Minor optimisations for cloud; some code changes required.
Repurchase The application is replaced by a SaaS product available on the sovereign platform.
Refactor The application is re-architected to be cloud-native and sovereign-compliant.
Relocate The application is moved to a different cloud region or sovereignty boundary.
